name: Complete Congenital Stationary Night Blindness, Schubert-Bornschein Type

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Electroretinographic Diagnostic Criteria for Complete CSNB

criteria.description: Characteristic electronegative electroretinogram (ERG) with normal a-wave and reduced b-wave amplitude
Congenital non-progressive night blindness with normal visual acuity
Normal fundus appearance without retinal degeneration
Family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic electronegative ERG and congenital night blindness with normal fundus
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can confirm mutations in genes such as NYX, GRM6, or TRPM1 associated with this condition.

pathognomonic.notes: Present from birth or early infancy
searchTerms: congenital inability to see in dark
eye electrical test showing negative pattern

common.symptomName: Reduced or absent rod-mediated visual function
searchTerms: poor night vision from rod dysfunction

common.symptomName: Normal visual acuity under photopic conditions

common.notes: Involuntary eye movements may be present

occasional.notes: Misalignment of the eyes may occur
Light sensitivity reported in some patients
Subtle defects in color discrimination possible
Variable cone dysfunction may be observed

rare.notes: Uncommon and usually mild if present

searchTerms: eye electrical test beyond typical patterns
minor changes in retina pigment layer

imaging: Normal retinal imaging (OCT and fundus photography) without degenerative changes
other: Electronegative ERG with preserved a-wave and reduced b-wave amplitude

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of residual rod function on ERG
Different ERG waveform with reduced a-wave
Progressive night blindness and peripheral vision loss
Characteristic fundus changes including bone spicule pigmentation

redFlags: Progressive vision loss instead of stationary course
Presence of retinal degeneration on fundus examination
references: Schubert G, Bornschein H. Stationäre Nachtblindheit mit negativem Elektroretinogramm. Klin Monatsbl Augenheilkd. 1952.
Dryja TP et al. Mutations in the NYX gene cause complete congenital stationary night blindness. Nat Genet. 2000.
Zeitz C, Robson AG, Audo I. Congenital stationary night blindness: an analysis and update of genotype-phenotype correlations and pathogenic mechanisms. Prog Retin Eye Res. 2015.
